 Judgment
1.

This is an appeal by the claimant claiming enhancement of the compensation awarded by the
Reference Court.

21.35 Ares of land was acquired from the claimant as per Section 4(1) Notification
dated 3
1.08.2006 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, for the purpose of (Japan Bank for International Cooperation) aided water supply scheme

. 
2. The Land Acquisition Officer awarded compensation fixing land value at the rate of Rs.7,082/-
per Are.

On reference, the Reference Court awarded compensation fixing land value at the rate of Rs. 9,310/- per cent relying on Ext.A1 document dated 03.05.2006, executed by a landowner in favour of the Requisitioning Authority, namely, water authority with respect to 14.36 Ares of land,
which was purchased for the very same purpose.
I heard the learned counsel for the appellant, Sri. Anchal C. Vijayan, the learned Senior Government Pleader Smt. Rekha C. Nair, who appeared for the 1st respondent.

sentences.text: 2 4. The learned counsel for the appellant contended that the Reference Court fixed the land value at the rate of Rs.9,310/- per cent finding of land value from the Ext.A1 document.
There is a specific finding in the judgment of the Reference Court itself that the acquired property is far better than the property involved in Ext.A1 sale deed.
The learned counsel further contended that it is in evidence from the commission report and evidence of the commissioner as AW2 that a part of the property is reclaimed.
The land involved in Ext. A1 is a wetland, and hence, a higher land value should have been given, at least for the 10 cents of land, which is found by the commissioner as reclaimed land.
On the other hand, the learned Government Pleader contended that the Section 4(1) Notification was in the year 2006, whereas the commissioner report was taken in the year 2016.
The nature and potentiality of the land might have been increased much within a period of 10 years, and on account of the acquisition also, the development in the area was boosted.
6. I have considered the rival contentions.
7. Ext.A1 is dated three months prior to Section 4(1) Notification by which the Requisitioning Authority purchased 14.36 Ares.
The land value works out to be Rs.9,310/- per cent.
Hence, the Reference Court awarded compensation fixing land value at the rate of Rs. 9,310/- per cent in the present case.

8. As rightly pointed out by the learned counsel for the appellant, there is a specific finding in the judgment of the Reference Court itself that the acquired property is far better than the property involved in Ext. A1 sale deed.
But how much is it 2025:KER:40364 LA.APP. NO. 6 OF 2017 better than Ext. A1 property, there is no specific evidence.

Even though the learned counsel for the appellant contended that a part of the property is filled up, the said evidence of the Advocate commissioner and Ext.C1 commission report could not be relied on, as the commission was taken nearly 10 years after the acquisition.
But the fact is that the acquired property is situated on the side of the road.

The advocate commissioner has specifically reported that the basic document relied on by the Land Acquisition Officer is situated 2 kilometers away from the acquired property and the Ext.A1 property is situated only 50 meters away from the acquired land.
9. Even if the developments in the area might have increased by the efflux of time, the nearness to the road, as stated by the advocate commissioner, could be relied on.

Considering the facts that the acquired property is having road frontage, the 2025:KER:40364 LA.APP. NO. 6 OF 2017 basic document could not be relied on and the finding of the Reference Court that the acquired property is better than Ext.A1 property
, I fix the land value of the acquired property at Rs.11,310/- per cent.
Accordingly, this appeal is allowed in part with proportional cost awarding an additional compensation of Rs. 2,000 per cent for the acquired land with all statutory benefits and interest.
